bolt-ksa-commercial.label: Saudi Arabia (commercial) — Jeddah & Eastern Province
bolt-ksa-commercial.summary: Saudi Arabia's two commercial waterfront metros — Jeddah on the Red Sea and the Eastern Province (Dammam / Khobar / Dhahran) on the Arabian Gulf — are dense, high-income urban-water markets served today only by congested coastal roads. Jeddah's Corniche and the new PIF waterfront are a continuous urban seafront; the Eastern Province corniche, Half Moon Bay and Tarout Island sit minutes apart by water but a slow drive apart by road, with Bahrain a short cross-Gulf hop away. This is a clean two-metro rollout — Jeddah first, then the Eastern Province — on a purpose-fit premium water tier, booked in the Bolt app.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Saudi Arabia (commercial)
hero.subtitle: Foil the Jeddah Corniche, then the Eastern Province coast, booked in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling tier across two Saudi commercial waterfronts — the Jeddah Corniche/PIF seafront first, then the Dammam–Khobar coast with a short cross-Gulf link to Bahrain.

bolt-ksa-commercial.why_now: Saudi Arabia's urban waterfronts are being rebuilt as walkable, mixed-use seafronts — the Jeddah Corniche and PIF's new Jeddah Central, and the Eastern Province corniche and island leisure belt. Both are dense, high-income, road-congested, and minutes apart by water. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears every leg in both metros, including the cross-Gulf Khobar–Manama hop. No giga-project timing risk: this is today's urban water in two proven cities.
bolt-ksa-commercial.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app: a Bolt car to the Corniche, a foiling hop down the seafront or across to Bahrain, a Bolt ride on arrival — a premium chain in the cities where Bolt is building regional density.
bolt-ksa-commercial.partner_context: Bolt is expanding its regional ambition. Jeddah and the Eastern Province are commercial, high-willingness-to-pay urban markets — deliberately scoped away from the sovereign giga-projects (NEOM, AMAALA, Red Sea Global) so the proposition is a clean, today-deliverable two-metro rollout, not a bet on resort-island ramp timing.
bolt-ksa-commercial.why_navier_now: Every leg is in Pioneer II range now: the Jeddah Corniche–Central seafront (2.4nm), the Jeddah Corniche–Yacht Club run (12nm), the Eastern Province corniche and island hops (8–13nm), and the cross-Gulf Khobar–Manama link (~18.6nm). Nothing here needs Quanta-LR to be real; the longer Gulf reach is a later, honestly-staged option.
bolt-ksa-commercial.differentiation: Against the coastal-road drive and the diesel water-taxi: faster, quiet, all-electric premium transfer on dense urban seafronts — aligned with both metros' waterfront-regeneration and sustainability branding.

proof_points.claim: Jeddah's waterfront is a continuous dense urban seafront.
proof_points.evidence: Jeddah Corniche–Central (PIF Jeddah Central) is ~2.4nm; Corniche–Yacht Club & Marina ~12nm; Corniche–Obhur marina belt ~16nm.

proof_points.claim: The Eastern Province coast is a minutes-by-water, slow-by-road metro.
proof_points.evidence: Dammam–Khobar corniche ~10nm; Khobar–Half Moon Bay ~13nm; Dammam–Tarout Island ~8nm.

proof_points.claim: Bahrain is a short cross-Gulf hop from the Eastern Province.
proof_points.evidence: Khobar/Dammam–Manama is ~18.6nm — well inside Pioneer II range, paralleling the King Fahd Causeway.

proof_points.claim: This is a commercial, today-deliverable market.
proof_points.evidence: Both metros are dense, high-income urban water served only by congested roads — no dependence on giga-project resort ramp.

objections.concern: Is this the NEOM / Red Sea giga-project pitch?
objections.response: No — we deliberately scoped those out. This is the commercial Jeddah and Eastern Province urban-water opportunity, deliverable on today's Pioneer II with no resort-ramp timing risk.

objections.concern: Why two metros on opposite coasts in one proposal?
objections.response: They are one commercial-KSA programme run as two clean, sequential rollouts — Jeddah first, the Eastern Province second — sharing brand, app, ops playbook and certification path, not one water network.

objections.concern: Is there real demand beyond leisure?
objections.response: Both seafronts mix corporate, residential and leisure water; we anchor on the densest urban legs first and let demand pull the network out.

bolt-ksa-commercial.the_ask: Co-brand a Saudi commercial water tier with Bolt — a 2-boat Pioneer II anchor on the Jeddah Corniche, then a second rollout across the Dammam–Khobar coast with a cross-Gulf link to Bahrain.
bolt-ksa-commercial.close: Two dense Saudi waterfront metros, both deliverable today — a Bolt-branded foiling tier that turns slow coastal drives into fast, quiet, in-app water lines.
bolt-ksa-commercial.end_state: A Jeddah Corniche network plus an Eastern Province coastal network with a cross-Gulf Bahrain link, all booked in the Bolt app.

bolt-estonia.label: Estonia — Tallinn HQ & the Nordic-Baltic triangle (Helsinki · Stockholm)
bolt-estonia.summary: Tallinn is Bolt's founding city and HQ — the natural flagship for Bolt-on-water. It sits on the Gulf of Finland with island and peninsula suburbs (Viimsi, Kakumäe, Prangli) far faster by water than by the long road loops, and it anchors a three-capital triangle: Tallinn–Helsinki (~43nm, the Baltic's busiest passenger sea corridor, inside Pioneer II range) and Tallinn/Helsinki–Stockholm across the archipelago (Quanta-LR roadmap). Launching in Bolt's home city is both a commercial play and the cleanest possible brand statement.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Tallinn & the Gulf of Finland
hero.subtitle: Foil across Tallinn Bay and up to Helsinki, booked in Bolt's home-city app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling tier across Tallinn Bay's suburbs and islands, with a Pioneer-range corridor north to Helsinki — launched in Bolt's founding city.

bolt-estonia.why_now: Tallinn's waterfront suburbs are growing and the Old City Harbour is a major cruise and ferry node. The Tallinn–Helsinki corridor carries millions of passengers a year on large diesel ferries. As Bolt's home market, Estonia is the natural flagship for a co-branded water tier. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears every Tallinn-Bay leg.
bolt-estonia.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app and wallet in the city where Bolt began: a Bolt car to the Old City Harbour, a foiling hop to Viimsi or across to Helsinki, a Bolt scooter on arrival.
bolt-estonia.partner_context: Bolt was founded and is headquartered in Tallinn and commands its deepest brand loyalty and operational density here. The Nordic-Baltic triangle — Tallinn HQ, the Pioneer-range Helsinki crossing, and the Stockholm archipelago — turns the home market into a flagship three-capital water network. A co-branded tier launched where Bolt began is the highest-signal demonstration of Bolt-on-water.
bolt-estonia.why_navier_now: Every Tallinn-Bay leg (Pirita 4.5nm, Viimsi 5nm) is well inside Pioneer II range, and the Tallinn–Helsinki crossing (43nm) is also within the 70nm envelope — a genuine near-term cross-Gulf corridor, not a roadmap aspiration.
bolt-estonia.differentiation: Against the suburban road loop: a direct water line that halves the journey with zero local emissions. Against the diesel Gulf ferry: faster and on-demand on the Helsinki run for time-sensitive riders.

proof_points.claim: Tallinn–Helsinki is the Baltic's busiest passenger sea corridor.
proof_points.evidence: Millions of annual passengers move between the two capitals on diesel ferries; the crossing is ~43nm.

proof_points.claim: Tallinn Bay suburbs are far faster by water.
proof_points.evidence: Viimsi and Kakumäe sit ~5–6nm across the bay versus long road loops around the inlets.

proof_points.claim: Estonia is Bolt's home market.
proof_points.evidence: Bolt was founded in Tallinn and has its deepest brand and operational density in Estonia.

proof_points.claim: Old City Harbour is a major maritime node.
proof_points.evidence: A leading cruise and ferry port providing a natural anchor terminal for a water tier.

objections.concern: The Baltic winter freezes the gulf.
objections.response: Yes — this is a strong shoulder/summer service. We right-size seasonally and concentrate on the ice-free months; the model assumes a seasonal operating window, not year-round.

objections.concern: Large ferries already run Tallinn–Helsinki cheaply.
objections.response: We add a premium speed-and-flexibility tier in the Bolt app for time-sensitive riders, not a replacement for the high-volume vehicle ferries.
Estonia's domestic market is modest, but the Gulf corridor and Bolt's home-market brand make it a high-signal flagship; we anchor with 2 boats and let demand pull scale.

bolt-estonia.the_ask: Launch a Bolt-branded water tier in Bolt's home city — a 2-boat Pioneer II anchor on Tallinn Bay, scaling onto the Pioneer-range Tallinn–Helsinki crossing and, on the Quanta-LR roadmap, the Stockholm archipelago to complete the Nordic-Baltic triangle.
bolt-estonia.close: There is no better place to prove Bolt-on-water than the city where Bolt was born — a compact home bay, a flagship Gulf crossing to Helsinki, and a three-capital triangle out to Stockholm.
bolt-estonia.end_state: A Tallinn Bay network plus a Pioneer-range cross-Gulf link to Helsinki, all booked in Bolt's home-city app.

bolt-thailand.label: Thailand — Phuket & Phang Nga (Andaman)
bolt-thailand.summary: Phuket and Phang Nga form the highest-density resort-and-island cluster in Southeast Asia, with a huge tourist island-hopping market today served by diesel speedboats and longtails. From the Phuket east-coast marinas, Phang Nga Bay's limestone karsts, Koh Yao, Phi Phi and Krabi all sit inside Pioneer II range, and the Andaman is calendar-predictable by monsoon half-year. Bolt is the leading challenger ride-hail brand in Thailand and is live in Phuket — a co-branded foiling tier turns the island-hop into a fast, clean, in-app service.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Phuket & the Andaman
hero.subtitle: Foil from the Phuket marinas out to Phang Nga, Phi Phi and Krabi, booked in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling island-hopping tier across the Andaman's densest resort cluster, anchored on the Phuket east-coast marina spine.

bolt-thailand.why_now: Phuket is one of the world's busiest island-tourism markets, and its day-trip and resort-transfer volume runs on aging diesel speedboats. Bolt is live in Phuket and is the main challenger to Grab in Thailand, so the app and the riders are already here. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears the entire core Andaman cluster; the monsoon calendar is predictable, and Phang Nga Bay is shielded year-round.
bolt-thailand.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app: a Bolt car from Phuket airport to the marina, a foiling hop to Koh Yao or Phi Phi, a Bolt ride on arrival — the island-hop folded into the trip people already book.
bolt-thailand.partner_context: Bolt has operated in Thailand since 2020 and is live in Phuket, Bangkok, Chiang Mai and beyond — the leading challenger to Grab. Phuket's tourist island-hopping demand is a textbook in-app water tier in a market where Bolt already has riders and brand.
bolt-thailand.why_navier_now: The core Andaman cluster is Pioneer II routine today: Phang Nga Bay (~12nm), Koh Yao Noi (~12nm), Phi Phi (~25nm), Krabi/Ao Nang (~30nm), even Similan (~50nm). The longer cross-coast and cross-border legs (Koh Samui ~190nm, Langkawi ~110nm) are honestly staged on Quanta-LR, never faked on a 70nm boat.
bolt-thailand.differentiation: Against the diesel speedboat and longtail: a quiet, stable, zero-wake foiling ride that is faster, cleaner and dramatically safer — in a market with real day-trip safety memory — all bookable in the Bolt app.

proof_points.claim: Phuket/Phang Nga is the densest resort-and-island cluster in SEA.
proof_points.evidence: Aman, Six Senses, Banyan Tree, Soneva, Anantara and dozens more anchor a huge day-trip island-hopping market.

proof_points.claim: The core Andaman cluster is inside Pioneer II range.
proof_points.evidence: Phang Nga Bay ~12nm, Koh Yao Noi ~12nm, Phi Phi ~25nm, Krabi ~30nm, Similan ~50nm.

proof_points.claim: Bolt is live in Phuket.
proof_points.evidence: Bolt has operated in Thailand since 2020 and lists Phuket among its active cities; it is the leading challenger to Grab.

proof_points.claim: Phang Nga Bay is a year-round operating window.
proof_points.evidence: The Phuket landmass shields Phang Nga Bay from the SW monsoon — calendar-predictable year-round operability.

objections.concern: Isn't this a luxury-charter play, not a Bolt play?
objections.response: The hospitality density is the backdrop; the Bolt wedge is the high-volume tourist island-hop — airport-to-marina-to-island in the app riders already use.

objections.concern: The SW monsoon degrades open crossings.
objections.response: True for exposed legs May–Oct — but Phang Nga Bay is shielded year-round and the calendar is predictable, so we right-size seasonally rather than pretend it away.
On short routes we compete head-to-head; our wedge is the Andaman cluster density plus the Quanta-LR cross-coast and cross-border reach (Samui, Langkawi) where the gap is widest.

bolt-thailand.the_ask: Co-brand an Andaman island-hopping water tier with Bolt — a 2-boat Pioneer II anchor on the Phuket east-coast marinas, scaling across Phang Nga, Phi Phi and Krabi.
bolt-thailand.close: Phuket is one of the world's great island-tourism markets, and Bolt already has the riders — a Bolt-branded foiling tier turns the diesel island-hop into a fast, clean, in-app signature ride.
bolt-thailand.end_state: A Phuket–Phang Nga island-hopping network with Pioneer II across the core cluster and a Quanta-LR cross-coast/cross-border roadmap, all booked in the Bolt app.

bolt-nigeria.label: Nigeria — Lagos (Lagos Lagoon)
bolt-nigeria.summary: Lagos is arguably the single largest urban water-commuter opportunity on earth — a ~20M+ megacity built around a lagoon, where short crow-flies trips take 2–3 hours across chronically gridlocked bridges. The Lagos State Waterways Authority (LASWA) already regulates a growing terminal network, but the lagoon carries a tiny fraction of trips on aging diesel boats. Bolt holds the largest ride-hail market share in Nigeria — a co-branded foiling lagoon-transit tier is a textbook congestion-beating overlay across the islands.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Lagos Lagoon
hero.subtitle: Foil across the lagoon — CMS to Victoria Island, Lekki and Ikorodu — booked in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling lagoon-transit tier that bypasses the bridges, anchored on the dense island CBD core and scaling onto the mass Ikorodu commuter corridor.

bolt-nigeria.why_now: Lagos State has made water transport a strategic priority for a decade and already has the regulator (LASWA) and terminals in place — the missing piece is a clean, fast, safe, reliable platform. Bolt has the largest market share in Nigeria and the riders already in-app. Pioneer II clears the entire core lagoon network today; the zero-wake stable foiling ride is itself the safety-and-trust story the lagoon needs.
bolt-nigeria.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app: a Bolt car to the CMS or Falomo terminal, a foiling hop across the lagoon to VI, Lekki or Ikorodu, a Bolt ride on arrival — the bridge-bypass folded into the daily commute.
bolt-nigeria.partner_context: Bolt holds the largest ride-hail market share in Nigeria (reported >60%), with Lagos its dominant city. An in-app lagoon-transit tier across the islands is a congestion-beating monetization layer in Bolt's single strongest African market.
bolt-nigeria.why_navier_now: The entire core lagoon network is in Pioneer II range today: CMS–Victoria Island (~1.5–4nm), Ikoyi–CMS (~2.5nm), CMS–Apapa (~4nm), and the mass-commuter flagship CMS–Ikorodu (~13nm). The longer growth corridors (Epe Free Zone ~30nm, Badagry ~28nm) are honestly staged on Quanta-LR.
bolt-nigeria.differentiation: Against the 2–3-hour bridge gridlock and the aging diesel ferry: a fast, clean, software-monitored, zero-wake platform whose stability and safety are the value proposition — the missing trust layer LASWA's network needs.

proof_points.claim: Lagos is the largest urban water-commuter opportunity on earth.
proof_points.evidence: A ~20–25M megacity built around a lagoon where road trips of a few km take 2–3 hours across a handful of jammed bridges.

proof_points.claim: The regulator and terminals already exist.
proof_points.evidence: LASWA regulates and is expanding terminals (CMS, Falomo, Ikorodu, Apapa, Badagry); a ready-made regulatory backbone.

proof_points.claim: The core lagoon network is inside Pioneer II range.
proof_points.evidence: CMS–VI ~1.5–4nm, CMS–Apapa ~4nm, CMS–Ikorodu ~13nm.

proof_points.claim: Bolt is Nigeria's largest ride-hail brand.
proof_points.evidence: Bolt holds the largest market share in Nigeria (reported >60%), with Lagos its dominant city.

objections.response: We run a tiered model: a high-WTP Victoria Island / Lekki corporate tier cross-subsidizes the mass Ikorodu commuter corridor — sustainable rollout economics in partnership with the state operator.

objections.concern: Lagoon debris and safety are real risks.
objections.response: Exactly the wedge: a stable, software-monitored, zero-wake foiling platform with rigorous training is safer and more reliable than the diesel incumbent — safety is the proposition, not a caveat.

objections.concern: Is the demand really there beyond pilots?
objections.response: The Ikorodu–CMS corridor is already the busiest existing ferry line; we anchor on proven flows and the high-WTP island CBD, not speculative routes.

bolt-nigeria.the_ask: Co-brand a Lagos lagoon-transit tier with Bolt — a 2-boat Pioneer II anchor on the island CBD core (CMS–VI–Ikoyi–Apapa), scaling onto the mass Ikorodu commuter corridor.
bolt-nigeria.close: Lagos wants to move onto the water, already has the regulator, and Bolt already has the riders — a Bolt-branded foiling tier is the clean, safe, fast platform that finally bypasses the bridges.
bolt-nigeria.end_state: A Lagos Lagoon network — island CBD core plus the Ikorodu mass-commuter corridor — with a Quanta-LR growth-corridor roadmap, all booked in the Bolt app.

bolt-south-africa.label: South Africa — Cape Town (Table Bay & False Bay)
bolt-south-africa.summary: Cape Town is Africa's premier coastal city, wrapped around Table Bay with the V&A Waterfront — one of the continent's most-visited destinations — as its anchor. The high-volume Robben Island heritage ferry, the Hout Bay and Simon's Town marine-wildlife harbours and the dramatic peninsula coastline make a natural premium leisure-and-heritage water market. Bolt is well established across South Africa; a co-branded foiling tier turns the waterfront and peninsula crossings into a fast, clean, in-app signature experience.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Cape Town
hero.subtitle: Foil from the V&A Waterfront to Robben Island and around the peninsula, booked in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling tier across Table Bay and False Bay — heritage crossings to Robben Island and premium peninsula leisure runs — anchored at the V&A Waterfront.

bolt-south-africa.why_now: Cape Town is a high-profile global tourism brand with huge waterfront footfall and a constant high-volume heritage ferry to Robben Island. Bolt is established across South Africa, so the app and riders are already here. Pioneer II clears the sheltered Table Bay and False Bay corridors; routing flexes around the Cape's wind exactly as the existing tour operators already do.
bolt-south-africa.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app: a Bolt car to the V&A Waterfront, a foiling crossing to Robben Island or a peninsula run to Hout Bay, a Bolt ride on arrival — the iconic Cape Town water experience, in-app.
bolt-south-africa.partner_context: Bolt is well established across South Africa (Cape Town, Johannesburg, Durban). Cape Town's premium tourism footfall and high willingness-to-pay make a co-branded heritage-and-leisure water tier a strong, brand-led African flagship.
bolt-south-africa.why_navier_now: The sheltered corridors are in Pioneer II range today: V&A–Robben Island (~7nm), V&A–Hout Bay (~12nm), Hout Bay–Simon's Town (~22nm) and Cape Town–Gordon's Bay (~30nm). Quanta-LR is held in reserve for the longer exposed-coast corridors — never faked on the all-electric boat.
bolt-south-africa.differentiation: Against the diesel tour boat: a faster, smoother, zero-emission crossing aligned with the Cape's marine-protected-area focus — and against the road, a premium peninsula link that skips the coastal drive, all in the Bolt app.

proof_points.claim: The V&A Waterfront is one of Africa's most-visited destinations.
proof_points.evidence: Huge baseline harbour-leisure footfall anchors the demand spine.

proof_points.claim: Robben Island is a constant high-volume heritage ferry.
proof_points.evidence: The UNESCO heritage crossing (~7nm) carries steady year-round demand.

proof_points.claim: The sheltered corridors are inside Pioneer II range.
proof_points.evidence: V&A–Robben Island ~7nm, V&A–Hout Bay ~12nm, False Bay hops ~22–30nm.

proof_points.claim: Bolt is established across South Africa.
proof_points.evidence: Bolt operates in Cape Town, Johannesburg and Durban as a leading e-hailing brand.

objections.concern: The Cape is famously windy and exposed.
objections.response: We route on the sheltered Table Bay and False Bay corridors and flex scheduling around the wind exactly as today's tour operators do; exposed-coast reach is held for Quanta-LR, not forced onto the all-electric boat.

objections.concern: Is this just a tourism novelty?
objections.response: Robben Island is a constant high-volume heritage line and the V&A draws huge year-round footfall — a real demand spine, with premium peninsula leisure on top.

objections.concern: Is the water-commuter case strong here?
objections.response: We are honest: Cape Town is a heritage-and-leisure tourism market, not a mass commuter one — that is exactly why it is scoped tier B as a brand-led African flagship.

bolt-south-africa.the_ask: Co-brand a Cape Town water tier with Bolt — a 2-boat Pioneer II anchor at the V&A Waterfront running the Robben Island heritage crossing and peninsula leisure links.
bolt-south-africa.close: Cape Town is a global tourism icon and Bolt already has the riders — a Bolt-branded foiling tier turns the V&A waterfront and the peninsula into a fast, clean, in-app signature experience.
bolt-south-africa.end_state: A Cape Town Table Bay and False Bay network — Robben Island heritage plus peninsula leisure — with a Quanta-LR exposed-coast reserve, all booked in the Bolt app.
